column1: # Per-destination deploy policy for `voipappz portal deploy`.
# A CATALOG, not conditionals. This was `$(filter mtn pbx20 nimbus,$(DEST))`
# twice over in the Makefile, and both rows below record a production incident
# — the kind of knowledge that has to be readable by whoever adds the fourth
# destination, at the moment they write config/deploy.<dest>.yml next door.
# Same reason config/services.tsv and config/deploy-manifest.tsv are files.
# scripts/check-portal-destinations.sh keeps this in step with the deploy files.
# dest      stop_first  healthcheck_url
# stop_first — the destination publishes a FIXED host port with `proxy: false`,
#   so the outgoing container still holds it when kamal starts the incoming one:
#       docker: Bind for 0.0.0.0:8888 failed: port is already allocated (125)
#   There is no proxy to hand traffic over, so the old container must let go
#   first; a few seconds of downtime is the cost of publishing a fixed port.
#   The default destination fronts with kamal-proxy and hands over cleanly —
#   stopping there would add an outage for nothing.
# healthcheck_url — where the post-deploy hook probes FROM THE DEPLOY BOX.
#   `-` means DELIBERATELY UNSET (the hook then skips itself), not "unknown".
#   mtn and pbx20 publish on 8888 behind someone else's nginx and firewall that
#   port off the public internet, so every probe returned 000 and failed a
#   deploy that had in fact succeeded. Verify those on the host instead:
#       ssh <host> 'curl -sk -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://127.0.0.1:8888/test'
#   nimbus IS probed: unlike the other two its 8888 answers from outside —
#   measured, not assumed. Skipping it is what let a TLS downgrade ship
#   unnoticed, so it gets the checks the others cannot have.
#   $PROD_URL reads that key from the portal's .env.
(default)
mtn
pbx20
nimbus
